results.cluster: Stop over-investing in advisory/lint review; ship capability before instruments
results.enforcer: none in this harness (claimed ESLint bulk suppressions live in app repos)
results.evidence: ESLint bulk suppressions are a tool in product repos, not in this dotfiles harness. In this repo, `eslint-suppressions` and `bulk-suppressions` appear only in docs/vets and an experiments file, not in a hook, test or workflow. Bulk suppressions would also only freeze lint debt. They would not enforce the behaviours 'ship capability before instruments' or 'freeze review loops'. No hook or test checks review-loop effort.

The index-budget lesson has an enforcer, but it is advisory. memory-audit.py emits a `WARN <project>: MEMORY.md at N/200 lines` line at >=70% of the load cap. The summary key is `index_over_budget`, not the claimed `index_over_cap`, and the note's `Name==stem is now a build refusal` claim found no matching code. A regression test covers the warning, but the audit never blocks. The eval-methodology and verification-pipeline lessons are prose only. I did not confirm that test_memory_audit.py runs in CI (grep of harness-tests.yml for it returned nothing).

results.cluster: Check git status before pulling in a launchpad; never bypass freshen refusal
results.evidence: launchpad-freshen.sh refuses to touch a launchpad that has rebase/merge in progress (line 106). It also refuses one with tracked modifications (line 117-118, 'not touched; rescue to a branch'), one with recent unpushed work (line 126-128), and one that cannot switch to the default branch (line 134-136). It only runs `git switch` after those checks pass. tests/launchpad-freshen-diagnosis.test.sh runs in CI (harness-tests.yml:1051-1052). Limits: the refusals print WARN and return, so they are script refusals rather than agent-blocking hooks. Nothing stops an agent from running `git pull` by hand in a launchpad. The script covers the freshen path, which is the failure the notes describe.
